solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plant putting oxygen in the sea

indicators.note: putting one thing in another says one piece goes inside the other
in tells where the oxygen symbol is placed: within the word for the sea

parts.note: the briny is a familiar name for the sea
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A gardener sets a plant into seawater with oxygen bubbled through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bryony is a climbing hedgerow plant, so the word is an example of a plant.

clue.text: It covers up British beating European

parts.note: athrob means throbbing or pulsing

explanation.surface: A British victory over a European, covered up.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe for after the bath wraps the body, a garment that keeps one covered.

clue.text: Not willing to get right off major road in US

indicators.note: off says the letter for right is taken away from the road name

parts.note: an interstate is a US highway linking states

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to come off a big American highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not willing' looks like reluctance but means without a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying intestate means dying without having made a legal will, hence not having made one.

clue.text: Identification upset person controlling admission

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gateman controls who comes in at a gate

explanation.surface: A doorman is annoyed while checking ID.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge with one's name on it identifies the wearer at an event.

clue.text: Shrink from sound one records

indicators.note: from sound says the answer is taken from how a word is spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist or psychoanalyst

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist backs away from a noise, someone keeping records.
explanation.definitionFit: An annalist writes annals, the year-by-year historical chronicles, so is a person who keeps records.

clue.text: Branch of science battling cancers pushily

indicators.note: battling suggests things being thrown about in a fight, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Science that fights tumours aggressively, as radiotherapy does.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of atomic nuclei is a field of physics, one discipline of science.

clue.text: Very hard old rocker

definitions.meaning: ... was a British new-wave pop star of the early 1980s

explanation.walkthrough: Adam Ant led Adam and the Ants, a hit British band around 1980.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant describes an unbreakably hard stone in legend and now someone utterly unyielding.

clue.text: Fool — I spot one being taken in

indicators.note: being taken in says the numeral is placed inside the word for spot

parts.note: a dot is a small spot
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone notices a gullible person being conned.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a stupid person, a simpleton, which is the sense of a fool.

clue.text: The American taxmen will get what belongs to them

parts.note: taken as written
the IRS is the US Internal Revenue Service

explanation.surface: The US tax authorities will claim people's property.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun stands for something owned by a group of other people.

clue.text: Onset of gremlins in foundries ruin cast with insignificant numbers discarded

indicators.note: in says the first letter of gremlins goes inside the rearranged letters
cast suggests metal poured into a new shape, so the letters are reshaped
the onset of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Mischievous gremlins wreck castings at metal works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges FOUNDRIES RUIN; the G from 'Onset of gremlins' goes 'in' that.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving a figure approximately means rounding it so small units are dropped.

clue.text: Carry before mass an object of veneration

indicators.note: before puts the carrying word ahead of the mass abbreviation

parts.note: to tote is to carry
m is the physics abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: Someone bears a sacred object ahead of the church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem or natural object revered by a clan, a thing held in reverence.

clue.text: Sweet juice in Oriental fruit

parts.note: nectar is the sweet liquid found in flowers
taken as written
E for East, as Oriental means eastern

explanation.surface: An exotic Eastern fruit full of sugary juice.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Stir too, cooking this

indicators.note: cooking suggests ingredients being mixed up, so the letters of the first two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: keep stirring while this dish cooks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: rearranging STIR TOO gives the dish, and constant stirring is what that rice dish needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish famous for needing constant stirring as it cooks.

clue.text: One soaking old ham

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
a ham is an overacting performer

explanation.surface: A retired overacting performer is drunk, or sits soaking in the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soaking' here is the slang sense of overcharging or fleecing someone, not getting wet.
explanation.definitionFit: An exactor demands payment, often excessively, and to soak someone is to extort money from them.

clue.text: Drop-outs in fifties obtain teenager to groom

indicators.note: to groom is to tidy and rearrange, so the letters of the two words are reordered

explanation.surface: A recruiter sets out to win over and prepare a young person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beat Generation were 1950s American writers and bohemians who rejected mainstream society.

clue.text: You and I in reference works solver uses endlessly

indicators.note: works as a verb means to knead or shape, so the letters are reworked
endlessly says the final letter of the two words is cut off

explanation.surface: The solver's use of reference books, keeps going without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last S of SOLVER USES; 'works' shuffles the remaining SOLVERUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The first-person plural pronoun covers the speaker plus the person addressed, us two.

clue.text: They may cause snoring noise Dad put out

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Father's racket disturbs everyone, keeping them awake at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlarged lymph tissue at the back of the nose blocks breathing and can cause loud breathing in sleep.

clue.text: Plastic explosive in America fatally damaged organ

indicators.note: in says the soft explosive pieces sit inside the name for America

parts.note: the New World is a name for the Americas
plastic means pliable, that is soft
HE stands for high explosive

explanation.surface: Semtex smuggled into the USA blew apart a vital body part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' is a newspaper, a mouthpiece; the 'fatal damage' was the 2011 phone-hacking scandal that closed this British Sunday tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is called an organ; this British Sunday paper closed in 2011 after the phone-hacking scandal.

clue.text: Leak reference in Daily Telegraph?

definitions.meaning: an escape of liquid seeping through
a newspaper cross-reference such as ... 5, split 3,4

explanation.walkthrough: Split 3,4 it is the instruction a paper gives to look elsewhere in its pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is liquid slowly escaping through a gap, which is a leak.

clue.text: Weapon held by Europe and America with most enthusiasm

indicators.note: held by says the weapon word is enclosed within the other piece

parts.note: the West means Europe and North America together
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A weapon shared by allies on both sides of the Atlantic, embraced eagerly.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmest means most cordial or ardent, showing the greatest eager feeling.

clue.text: Bird pecked tasty morsel

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
bit, past tense of bite, means pecked

explanation.surface: A small bird nibbled a delicious snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a small choice piece of food, a dainty delicacy.

clue.text: One old instrument sent back hint of German threat to shipping

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: sent back says the instrument's name is read from right to left

parts.note: a rebec is a medieval bowed stringed instrument

indicators.note: a hint of a word is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A wartime warning: an old weapon returned, a sign of German menace at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating masses of ice endanger ships, famously the Titanic, so they menace vessels.

clue.text: Fine Australian shrub

parts.note: an eric was the blood-fine a killer paid the victim's family under old Irish law

explanation.surface: A handsome bush from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' is a noun here, the eric, a fine paid for murder under ancient Irish Brehon law.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the genus of heaths and heathers, low evergreen bushes.

clue.text: One working in theatre: a jerk on a rope performing

parts.note: in sailing, a surge is a sudden jerk or slackening of a rope
on means performing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: An actor or stagehand tugs on a rope during a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests a stage but means an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Operations are performed in a hospital's operating theatre, where this doctor works.

clue.text: Rattletrap's part of rubric: abracadabra!

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A magician's incantation in a book's heading suggests a rattling contraption.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattletraps are rickety knick-knacks or curios, the odds and ends of ornaments and junk.

clue.text: I've no excited last words

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone says they feel no thrill at all.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoi is the short closing stanza of a poem, its concluding lines.

clue.text: Farceur gets English cross

parts.note: Ben Travers was a writer of the famous Aldwych farces

explanation.surface: A comic playwright becomes an Englishman crossing over.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Travers (1886-1980) wrote the Aldwych farces staged in London in the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across or pass over something, so it is a verb meaning to go over.

clue.text: Secret police's arrest

definitions.meaning: the Stasi were East Germany's secret police; with the possessive the apostrophe is dropped
a stoppage or standstill, as in cardiac arrest

explanation.walkthrough: Drop the apostrophe from the possessive of the East German secret police to get the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of stoppage or inactivity, the sense of arrest as a halting of motion.
